item.description:
Dorian Menard
Research summary of 2,400 answers from Google AI Overviews, Google AI Mode, ChatGPT and Gemini to 200 commercial questions about 20 Perth industries, asked three times between 8 and 10 September 2026. Most recommended businesses sat outside the Google Maps top 20, recommendations changed from day to day, and the businesses recommended repeatedly tended to rank in Google's organic top 10 and carry more Google reviews. item.title: The AI Citation-Recommendation Gap: Citations and Business Recommendations in Google AI Mode and AI Overviews, Perth 2026 (Research Summary)
item.description:
Dorian Menard
In 1,942 Google AI answers to 200 questions about 20 Perth industries (9 to 13 November 2026), 91.1% of Google AI Mode business recommendations came with no citation to the business's own website. Being cited and being recommended depended mostly on the type of question, and recommendations changed from day to day. A plain-English summary of how to measure AI visibility properly. item.title: py-pdfconform
item.description:
Nicolás Vaughan
py-pdfconform converts PDF files to two ISO standards: PDF/A, for long-term archiving (PDF/A-1b, PDF/A-2b and PDF/A-3b), and PDF/X-4, for printing. It is a single Python script, py-pdfconform.py. The conversion itself is done by Ghostscript; pikepdf opens encrypted or damaged files before it, and corrects the metadata after it. DNA-based disaster victim identification is commonly performed sequentially, with matches accepted before all genetic evidence is considered jointly. However, early matches may be incorrect or inconsistent with the globally most likely assignment, and treating them as final can affect subsequent identifications. item.title: An algorithm for solving structured problems involving $L$-infimal convolutions
item.description:
Cong Bang Vu, Xuan Nham Vu
We develop an operator-splitting framework for solving structured minimization problems involving linear compositions of $L$-infimal convolutions. We introduce a primal-dual shadow Douglas-Rachford splitting method and establish its convergence. As a result, we derive a fully primal-dual splitting algorithm for the class of the aforementioned minimization problems.

The cost combines tracking terms, a quadratic control cost and an $L^1$ term promoting sparsity in time.
